minutes.headline: Assessors unanimously ratified Susan Byrne as principal assessor and discussed troubled software conversion and switching vendors.
minutes.summary: The Board of Assessors met remotely, approved prior minutes, ratified the town manager's appointment of Susan Byrne as principal assessor, and voted to ratify the town counsel's response to an Open Meeting Law complaint. Most of the meeting dealt with shortcomings in the Tyler software conversion and whether to consider switching to Vision; no decision was made, with a follow-up meeting planned once the new assessor starts.

votes.motion: Approve the minutes of the April 8 and April 13 meetings.
Approve (ratify) the appointment of Susan Byrne as principal assessor.
Ratify the Open Meeting Law complaint response letter prepared by town counsel and send it to the Attorney General.

budget_items.what_was_said: The town is moving from a long-time outside vendor to a full-time principal assessor.
A member was unsure of the vendor's obligations for the conversion since it was no longer being paid; the response said it would correct issues even though no longer under contract.
Members said a vendor change would come down to finances, including the cost of the state contract versus alternatives.

decisions.decision: The town manager will email the vendor's manager asking for a timeline for finishing the conversion fixes and copy the board.
Board agreed to schedule a meeting soon after Susan Byrne starts to get her view on the software system.
A member was asked to contact Vision sales staff to learn what a Vision conversion would cost.

what_happened.line: The Board of Assessors voted unanimously to ratify the town manager's appointment of Susan Byrne as principal assessor.
The board moved to ratify town counsel's Open Meeting Law complaint response for the Attorney General; the result of that vote was not audible.
Most of the meeting covered shortcomings in the Tyler software conversion and whether to consider switching to Vision; no decision was made.
The town manager will email the outgoing vendor's manager for a timeline to finish the conversion fixes, copying the board.
A member will ask Vision sales staff what a conversion would cost, and a meeting is planned soon after Byrne starts.

why_it_matters: Property assessments and tax bills depend on the assessing software, so unfinished conversion fixes can affect how reliably values are produced.
Moving from an outside vendor to a full-time principal assessor changes how assessing is staffed, and a software switch would add a cost that the town budget, mostly taxes, would carry.
watch_next: A board meeting soon after Susan Byrne starts, to hear her view on the software system.
The vendor's timeline for finishing the conversion fixes, and the Vision cost estimate.
